sheets: L-100 Landscape and Tree Canopy Plan (2 of 3)

gradingVerification.method: Measured on the proposed surface itself, not asserted from design intent. Front yard: a grid outside the drainage apron, fall read toward the street and as steepest descent. Perimeter: rays off every wall, 10 ft out, checked for reversal and for the fall the county note promises. Toe: the fall built into the apron toe, which is what carries away water arriving from uphill ground.
gradingVerification.result: PASS on all four lots, after the design changes
gradingVerification.note: "Beyond the apron sheds toward the house" counts ground standing ABOVE the pad — a bank, not a defect. What makes it safe is that the apron toe has fall, so what arrives there is carried away instead of standing against the foundation.

openItems: LABEL COLLISIONS are the largest remaining drafting defect. Lot and easement labels, frontage dimensions, the planting strip note and the apron note overprint each other and the bearings in several places. The sheet has no label-placement or collision-avoidance pass. This was invisible until the review rasteriser was given the standard font data — every earlier check in this thread was reading a text-free render.
LOT 54 reaches 39% (2.6:1) and LOT 55 40% (2.5:1) at the rear tie-out. Both are flatter than the 2:1 limit for a stabilised slope and are specified in ground cover, with the limit drawn.

SLOPING THE PAD DID NOT CUT THE IMPORT. 4,740 CY level against 4,775 CY sloped — the pad and its apron are a small part of a regrade dominated by the front-yard fill, which is what the 2 ft finished floor above the street costs on lots that fall away from the road. Lowering the finished floor is the lever that would move it, and that is a decision above this drawing.
Stoop stands 0.13 to 0.60 ft off the dwelling face on Lots 54, 55 and 56 — drawn square to the frontage while the house is square to itself. Under drafting tolerance at 1" = 20'.
Field-run topographic survey outstanding; existing grade is county 2 ft lidar contour mapping. Swale inverts are set from it and must be reset from the field survey.

designChanges: RETAINING WALL REMOVED from Lot 55 per instruction. The 3 ft wall 22 ft behind the dwelling is gone; the rear tie-out runs at its natural steepness and is stabilised with ground cover.

PAD SLOPED per instruction. It was a level plane at finished floor less 0.5 ft; it now falls at 2% front-to-rear, square to the dwelling, from the finished-floor datum at the high end. The apron toe inherits that fall and so has an outlet at the low corner.
GROUND COVER specified for slopes steeper than 3:1, with the limit line drawn on the plan and a legend entry. Lot 53 has 4 limit lines, Lot 54 five, Lot 55 three; Lot 56 none.
SWALE INVERT PROFILE solved across the network and printed — invert in and out on every reach label, in the schedule, and in the grade control schedule beside the ground elevation.
CONTOURS regenerated: saddles resolved by cell centre, chaining tolerance cut from 3.6 ft to 0.001 ft, cell 6 ft to 3 ft, Chaikin smoothing.

LABEL PLACEMENT. Annotations were written the instant their geometry was drawn, at a fixed offset, so on a four-lot sheet they overprinted each other. They are now queued with an anchor, a preferred position and a ladder of fallbacks, and placed in one pass after all geometry: highest priority first, each taking the first position that does not overlap something already on the paper, with a leader drawn when a label has to move far from what it names.

LOT 54 REAR YARD. The rear transition ran 40 ft off the pad and then met existing ground, so the proposed contours behind the dwelling were a tight band a few feet off the wall. The rear apron now carries out as a level bench — 21 ft at 2% — with the 9.2 ft drop taken in the 28 ft beyond it at 33%. Sized against two computed bounds: the nearest RECORDED easement (57 ft) less an 8 ft standoff, and the depth left to the tie line (69 ft). Steepest slope eased 39% to 37%.

LANDSCAPE SHEET L-100 added as sheet 2, carrying the easement areas, the trees, the planting strip and a new TREE CANOPY SCHEDULE. The bottom band is now routed by sheet: the soils table and storm drain schedule stay on the civil sheets, the canopy schedule is on the landscape one.

TITLE BLOCK: all four addresses instead of the subject address alone; jurisdiction spelled "Prince George's County, Maryland" instead of the slug "prince georges md"; "(AUTOMATED)" dropped from DRAWN BY; DESIGNED BY and CHECKED BY left blank instead of carrying an instruction to the reader in a field meant for a name.

ADJOINING LOT LINES were trimmed by their ENDPOINTS, so a call running three hundred feet from a corner near the frontage was drawn whole — down the sheet and through the schedules. The reach is now applied along the line. The plan is also clipped to its own viewport, so nothing can enter the table or detail bands again.

L-100 WAS THE GRADING PLAN WITH A CANOPY SCHEDULE UNDER IT. 29 of the 68 Contour features in the model are proposed:true, and `Contour` sat in the composer BASE list, so the grading design printed on every sheet. subjectForFeature already routed a proposed contour to grading_design — the blanket kind test ahead of it meant nothing ever asked. Existing contours now go everywhere as context; proposed ones only where grading is a subject of the sheet.

BASEMENT / FINISHED FLOOR / SUBFLOOR blocks were printing inside every dwelling on the landscape sheet. They are grading data and are now drawn only on C-001 and C-400. The address stays on all three — it says which house this is, which every discipline needs.

ADJOINER REACH 95 ft to 220 ft. 95 was set while the reach was applied to a segment's ENDS and was doing two jobs — how much neighbour to show, and keeping long calls out of the schedules. The viewport clip does the second job now, so the reach only has to do the first, and at 95 ft measured ALONG the line the lots across Fort Foote Road were stubs.

COUNTY MANUALS INSTALLED at docs/site-plan-reference/landscape/ — Landscape Manual (Dec 2010), Environmental Technical Manual (2010) and Part D (2018), the county tree canopy worksheet, and CB-021-2024. Text extracted beside each PDF, checksums, and a SOURCES.md.

STORM DRAIN SIZE 42 → 48 IN across the culvert, the easement extension and the outfall. See stormDrainSizing for the inlet/outlet control analysis. Three sheet notes hardcoded "42 IN" and now read the size from the model, so the drawing cannot drift from the design again.

swmConceptApproval.question: Does the latest plan generation pass SWM concept approval?
blocking: NO ESD PRACTICE IS SIZED OR DRAWN. WQv is computed at 924 cf across the four lots and nothing treats it; SWMPractice features in the model: 0. Every lot carries omitSwmPractice: true. The Maryland Stormwater Management Act of 2007 requires ESD to the Maximum Extent Practicable BEFORE structural conveyance, and the set demonstrates neither the practice nor the MEP case.

THE SWALE IS A CONVEYANCE, NOT A CREDITED PRACTICE. It is designed and checked for capacity, normal depth, velocity and freeboard. A grass swale can earn ESD credit under the MDE Design Manual, but only with the media, ponding depth, drawdown and Pe computations that are not here.

THE OUTFALL IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The reach below the system low point leaves the property and crosses adjoining land with no easement of record, and the county mapping shows it RISING 1.0 ft. A concept needs a demonstrated point of discharge.
alsoOutstanding: Existing grade is county 2 ft lidar contour mapping, not a field-run topographic survey. The swale inverts and any outfall analysis rest on it.
Runoff coefficients use a lawn C of 0.25 without tying it to the SSURGO hydrologic soil group, which the drainage assumptions already flag.
whatItDoesCarry: Drainage area map and computations per lot — rational method, NOAA Atlas 14 Vol. 2 Ver. 3.
Pre and post peak discharge with the increase to be managed: 0.88 cfs across the four lots.
WQv by the Maryland Stormwater Design Manual on a 1.0 in rainfall.
A conveyance system with hydraulics, invert profile and a grade control schedule.

stormDrainSizing.decision: 48 in RCP CL IV — revised from 42 in.
stormDrainSizing.appliesTo: The whole run: the Fort Foote Road culvert, the 162 ft extension in the recorded 60 ft storm drain easement on the Lot 54 / Lot 55 party line, and the outfall. A 48 in discharging into a 36 in is worse than doing nothing.
stormDrainSizing.watershed: 39.1 ac at the culvert, C = 0.40. Q10 = 71.9 cfs, Q100 = 94.9 cfs.
stormDrainSizing.why: 48 in is the knee of the marginal-gain curve. It takes Q100 utilisation from 91% (no margin) to 64%, drops velocity 9.87 → 7.55 fps, and moves control from the INLET to the OUTLET — the point at which the barrel is actually being used rather than throttled by its inlet. It delivers 4.23 ft of headwater reduction against existing, versus 2.97 ft for a 42 in, which is the floodplain mitigation itself.
conditions: COVER. 48 in OD is 4.83 ft, so finished grade must be at least invert + 6.33 ft — 0.58 ft deeper than a 42 in. Confirm against the surveyed invert through a rear easement where existing ground is EL 46–48. If cover cannot be held, 42 in with an enlarged inlet is the fallback and still buys 2.97 ft.
INLET ENLARGEMENT IS NOT OPTIONAL. Inlet control governs at 36 in and 42 in; the 48 in only reaches outlet control with the inlet enlarged to suit.
Inverts and slope to be set from the field-run topographic survey.
stormDrainSizing.engineFix: Wall thickness was hardcoded at 4 in — right for a 42 in barrel, wrong for a 48 in. Every OD and cover figure would have been 0.17 ft short on the one dimension that decides whether the pipe fits under the rear yard. It now scales with the barrel.
